key_insight: VersaCamVLA makes robotic VLA policies adaptable to changing camera setups, instead of depending on one fixed training configuration. It learns a camera-agnostic scene representation so the same policy can work across different numbers, positions, and poses of cameras.
problem_solved: Standard VLA models for robotic manipulation are brittle when the camera configuration changes at deployment. This includes changes in camera count, viewpoint, or pose that were not seen during training.
method: Decouples camera-set representation from action prediction, so visual input handling is separated from control learning.
Learns a unified scene-token interface that converts an arbitrary set of posed RGB views into a consistent representation.
Uses this camera-configurable representation to support variable sensor setups without retraining a separate policy for each camera arrangement.
impact: This helps researchers and practitioners deploy manipulation policies in real-world robotics settings where camera setups are rarely fixed. It improves robustness and flexibility, reducing the need for expensive reconfiguration-specific training.

paper_title: VersaCamVLA: Camera-Configurable VLA Policies for Robotic Manipulation
paper_authors: Boyao Han, Chen Shi, Jingjing Qian, ZhuoTan Tian, Li Jiang
